clue.text: Draw attention to tirade that's outrageous

parts.note: to flag something is to mark it out for notice
a rant is a long angry outburst

explanation.surface: Someone shouts an outrageous tirade to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant conduct is shockingly blatant, glaringly offensive.

clue.text: Guy 'always supports Midlands club

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece below holds up the one above, so it comes after it

parts.note: Nottingham Forest is a football club in the English Midlands
AY is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A man who has always followed a Midlands football team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is a guy rope; Nottingham Forest is a Midlands football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A forestay is a rope or cable bracing a ship's mast forward, a kind of stay.

clue.text: Fine and bail armed crook

indicators.note: crook is read as bent or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A court sets a fine and bail for an armed criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like the criminal but signals that BAIL ARMED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something admirable is excellent, very good indeed.

clue.text: Girl got up about one

indicators.note: the word for got up goes about, around, the letter for one

parts.note: rose is the past of rise, to get up
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl got up at about one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a girl's name.

clue.text: Making a mistake in giving agreement

definitions.meaning: from 'even Homer nods', a lapse of attention causing an error
moving the head down and up to say yes

explanation.surface: Someone errs by agreeing too readily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer sometimes nods' is the saying that even the best make slips.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozing off into error and bowing the head in assent are both described by the same word.

clue.text: Swore love on the Bible, and married

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so love comes after the Bible

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A bride and groom take their vows on the Bible and are married.
explanation.definitionFit: To have avowed something is to have declared it solemnly, as an oath.

clue.text: Break rule 'on vet for Terrier, perhaps

indicators.note: break means smash up, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A dog breaks a rule on the vet's table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrier' is not a dog but a member of the Territorial Army, a part-time British reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Territorial Army are part-time unpaid soldiers who enlist freely.

clue.text: Drink I got from steward

indicators.note: the letter I is got, that is taken, from the word for steward

parts.note: a waiter is a steward who serves food and drink

explanation.surface: I got a drink from the steward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got from' looks like receiving, but here I is removed from WAITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the most basic drink.

clue.text: Trim material, having stuff to put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so both pieces read from the bottom

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
to pad is to stuff

explanation.surface: A neat bit of fabric is used to stuff and hang up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put up' reverses REPPAD in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapper describes a neat, smartly turned-out person.

clue.text: Artist manages' to capture pair pre-eminent in beauty

indicators.note: the word for manages takes in, captures, the letters picked

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: the leading pair of letters, those first in the word beauty

explanation.surface: An artist manages to paint a couple of striking beauties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair pre-eminent in beauty' gives BE, the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was a Flemish Baroque painter.

clue.text: Rejecting old civilisation, he helped found another

indicators.note: rejecting is taken as turning back, so the ancient civilisation's name is read from its end

parts.note: Sumer was the ancient civilisation of southern Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A man turns his back on an ancient culture to found a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus and his twin Romulus were the legendary founders of Rome, the 'another' civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend the twins raised by a she-wolf founded the city of Rome.

clue.text: Score twice with one dart?

parts.note: in darts the narrow ring at the top of the board doubles twenty, so one throw scores forty, twice the top single score

explanation.definitionFit: A double top is the outer ring segment of the twenty on a dartboard, worth two times twenty.

clue.text: Help the enemy, so go to prison

parts.note: to serve someone is to help or assist them
time is proverbially 'the enemy', as in 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: A traitor helps the enemy and so ends up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a collaborator; 'the enemy' is the old saying that time is everyone's foe.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve time is the idiom for spending a sentence in jail.

clue.text: Carefully treat fish

definitions.meaning: to tend a patient or nurture something with care
the ... shark (and ... hound) is a kind of fish

explanation.surface: Someone tends a fish with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend the sick is the verb sense; a nurse shark gives the fish sense.

clue.text: On country walk, run away? Not hurrying at all

indicators.note: run away is read as the abbreviation for run going away from the word

parts.note: rambling is walking for pleasure in the countryside
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: On a walk in the country, the walker flees, quite unlike a leisurely stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run away' looks like a single verb but splits: R for run is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, leisurely pace.

clue.text: Some universities have female football competition

parts.note: Ivy is a woman's name
a league is a competition between clubs

explanation.surface: Some colleges field women's football competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is a group of old American universities such as Harvard and Yale.

clue.text: Keeping quiet about passion, in case

indicators.note: the letters for quiet go about, that is around, the word for passion

parts.note: SH is the call for silence
heat is intensity of feeling

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their passion secret, just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover or case, as for a sword blade.

clue.text: Will it hold only a fraction of the crop?

definitions.text: Will it hold only a fraction of the crop?

parts.words: Will it hold only a fraction of the crop?
parts.note: describes a farm building that stored the tenth of the harvest paid to the church

explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn stored the tenth of produce owed as church tax.

clue.text: Heard nervous girl joined plain-living Americans

indicators.note: heard tells us the words are taken as spoken, by their sound

parts.note: shy means nervous, and Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A timid girl joined an austere American community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain-living' is a pun on the Great Plains where the Cheyenne lived, not frugality.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Scot's refusal to back African

annotationWithheld.why: Scot's refusal to back African (6): KENYAN reads as KEN + reversed NAY, but no clue word gives KEN except 'Scot's', which would need a word for 'know' the clue lacks; scan confirms the text

clue.text: To sleep, people provided some linen

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
kin are one's people, relatives

explanation.surface: Relatives provide some bed linen for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Table napkins are part of household linen.

clue.text: Minor injury is no handicap

definitions.meaning: a small scrape on the skin from a claw or thorn
in golf a player who plays off zero handicap is described by this word

explanation.surface: A small graze is no hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A light graze is the injury sense; a golfer playing off zero is the handicap sense.

clue.text: Caught in tin, insect bit

indicators.note: the insect is caught inside the chemical symbol for tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a midge is a tiny biting fly

explanation.surface: An insect bit someone after being caught in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like the past of bite but is the noun, a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a tiny amount.

clue.text: Remiss, to let the French get out of touch

indicators.note: the French article is made to get out, leave, the word for remiss

parts.note: remiss means careless
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone careless lets the French slip out of contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of touch' reads as a phrase, but 'touch' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle, loving touch.

clue.text: Prize awarded by Paris that inspired Newton

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth Paris gave the golden fruit to Aphrodite as the fairest goddess
the fruit said to have fallen near Newton and prompted his theory of gravity

explanation.surface: A Paris award once sparked a scientist's great idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is not the city but the Trojan prince who judged the goddesses.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden fruit of the Judgement of Paris and the falling fruit of the gravity story are the same kind of fruit.

clue.text: Running track soundly put together

indicators.note: soundly means by sound, so the word for put together is heard

parts.note: pieced means assembled

explanation.surface: A running track is built properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'firmly' but signals a homophone of PIECED, said 'peest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a prepared ski run.

clue.text: In which boy may collect a set, discarding duplicate?

definitions.text: In which boy may collect a set, discarding duplicate?

parts.words: In which boy may collect a set, discarding duplicate?
parts.note: describes a hobby of gathering a complete series of postage stamps and swapping away any spare copies

explanation.definitionFit: Philately is the hobby of collecting and studying postage stamps.

clue.text: Bore in a very big river losing height

indicators.note: losing tells us the abbreviation for height is dropped

parts.note: huge means very big

explanation.surface: A bore in a vast river loses height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tidal wave on a river but is a drilling tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a tool for boring holes.

clue.text: Liberal sort of synagogue I entered instead of university

indicators.note: sort is read as a verb, to rearrange, so the altered word's letters are shuffled
the letter I goes in where the letter for university stood

explanation.surface: A liberal kind of synagogue lets someone in instead of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: In SYNAGOGUE the U becomes I, giving SYNAGOGIE, which 'sort of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy-going person is relaxed and tolerant, a liberal outlook.

clue.text: Good weather for crop

parts.note: rain is a kind of weather

explanation.surface: Fine weather is good for growing crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal crops such as wheat and barley are harvested as this.

clue.text: Become mad as Macbeth did, looking at his hands?

definitions.text: as Macbeth did, looking at his hands?
definitions.meaning: Macbeth stares at the blood on his hands after the murder, perceiving the colour of blood

explanation.surface: Macbeth goes mad staring at his bloody hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's temper is the idiom; to perceive crimson literally is the joke sense.

clue.text: Door right into new canteen

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the rearranged word
new suggests the word made fresh, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A door on the right leads into the new canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns CANTEEN into ENTANCE, and R goes 'into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is a way in to a building or room.
